title_en: Wuhu Huarong Xingshang Investment Partnership (Limited Partnership) v. Huangshan Huangshan District Mingren International Artist Manor Real Estate Co., Ltd. et al. — dispute over a loan contract
ruling_gist_en: Whether a partnership files a lawsuit over disputes arising from its operations constitutes a relatively significant operational matter of the partnership and cannot be simply classified as a routine affair in business activities. If the partnership agreement does not prescribe a clear voting method for such matters, and the managing partner(s) of the partnership disagree on the matter, applying the capital majority rule for voting is not conducive to protecting the interests of small and medium investors, nor does it reflect the personal nature of the partnership. Pursuant to Article 30 of the Partnership Enterprise Law of the People's Republic of China, the voting method shall be one vote per partner, and a resolution shall be passed by more than half of all partners.
keywords_en: civil; dispute over loan contract; second instance; Supreme People's Court; Anhui Province; Beijing City; Jiangsu Province; Shanghai City; legal person; natural person; foreign-invested enterprise; Partnership Enterprise Law; voting method for partnership litigation; authority of managing partner; capital majority rule versus one vote per person; affirm the original judgment; loan contract; partnership; managing partner; voting rights dispute; passage by more than half with one vote per person; contract dispute; industry Co., Ltd. and other loan contract disputes
full_text_en:
Wuhu Huarong Xingshang Investment Partnership (Limited Partnership) v. Huangshan Huangshan District Mingren International Artists Manor Real Estate Co., Ltd. et al.

— Dispute over Loan Contract

[Ruling Summary]

Whether a partnership should file a lawsuit over a dispute arising in the course of its operations is a significant operational matter of the partnership and cannot be simply classified as an ordinary matter in daily business activities. If the partnership agreement does not specify a clear voting method for such a matter, and when the managing partners of the partnership disagree on such a matter, applying a capital majority voting rule for a resolution is not conducive to protecting the interests of small investors and cannot reflect the human capital nature of the partnership. Therefore, in accordance with the provisions of Article 30 of the Partnership Enterprise Law of the People's Republic of China, a voting method of one vote per partner and approval by more than half of all partners shall be adopted.

Civil Ruling of the Supreme People's Court

(2022) Supreme People's Court Final Civil No. 145

Appellant (Plaintiff at First Instance): Wuhu Huarong Xingshang Investment Partnership (Limited Partnership). Principal place of business: Room 17170, 17th Floor, Binjiang Business Building, No. 1 Guanlan Road, Jinghu District, Wuhu City, Anhui Province.

Managing Partner: Huarong Emerging Industry Investment Management Co., Ltd. (formerly Huarong Emerging Industry Investment Management Co., Ltd.). Domicile: Room 228, Building 5, No. 25 Shuntong Road, Shunyi District, Beijing.

Agent ad litem: Tian Dapeng, lawyer of Beijing Deheheng Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Quan Jing, trainee lawyer of Beijing Deheheng Law Firm.

Appellee (Defendant at First Instance): Huangshan Huangshan District Mingren International Artists Manor Real Estate Co., Ltd. Domicile: Taling, Taipinghu Town, Huangshan District, Huangshan City, Anhui Province.

Litigation Representative: Anhui Zhongwan Law Firm, administrator of Huangshan Huangshan District Mingren International Artists Manor Real Estate Co., Ltd.

Agent ad litem: Wang Tao, lawyer of Anhui Zhongwan Law Firm.

Appellee (Defendant at First Instance): Nanjing Longchang Real Estate Development Group Co., Ltd. Domicile: Unit C1, 21st Floor, Building B, Jinshan Building, No. 24 Shanxi Road, Gulou District, Nanjing City, Jiangsu Province.

Legal Representative: Zhu Jinlong, Chairman of the Board of the company.

Appellee (Defendant at First Instance): Zhu Jinlong, male, born on January 13, 1953, Han ethnicity, domiciled at Gulou District, Nanjing City, Jiangsu Province.

Appellee (Defendant at First Instance): Zhang Jianhe, female, born on June 28, 1959, Han ethnicity, domiciled at Baixia District, Nanjing City, Jiangsu Province.

Appellee (Defendant at First Instance): China Zhongshi Financial Group Limited (China Gem Financial Group Limited). Domicile: Flat/Rm 2606C, 26/F, Bank of America Tower, 12 Harcourt Road, Central, Hong Kong Special Administrative Region.

Litigation Representative: Liu Jieshan, Director of the company.

Appellee (Defendant at First Instance): Liu Jieshan, male, born on October 30, 1973, resident of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region.

Third Party at First Instance: Huarong Emerging Industry Investment Management Co., Ltd. (formerly Huarong Emerging Industry Investment Management Co., Ltd.). Domicile: Room 228, Building 5, No. 25 Shuntong Road, Shunyi District, Beijing.

Legal Representative: Zhou Li, Chairman of the Board of the company.

Third Party at First Instance: Wuhu Huarong Xingrong Investment Partnership (Limited Partnership). Principal place of business: Room 17167, 17th Floor, Binjiang Business Building, No. 1 Guanlan Road, Jinghu District, Wuhu City, Anhui Province.

Managing Partner: Huarong Emerging Industry Investment Management Co., Ltd. (formerly Huarong Emerging Industry Investment Management Co., Ltd.). Domicile: Room 228, Building 5, No. 25 Shuntong Road, Shunyi District, Beijing.

Third Party at First Instance: Zhongshi Enterprise Development (Jiangsu) Co., Ltd. Domicile: 2nd Floor, Wei Ji Zhan, No. 3 Shizheng Road, Shiye Town, Dantu District, Zhenjiang City, Jiangsu Province.

Legal Representative: Fang Yitao, Executive Director of the company.

Agent ad litem: Fang Liqing, lawyer of Beijing Bairui Law Firm.

Third Party at First Instance: Qinlai Investment Asset Management (Shanghai) Co., Ltd. Domicile: Room 4141, 4th Floor, No. 35 Rijing Road, China (Shanghai) Pilot Free Trade Zone.

Legal Representative: Yang Huaijun, Executive Director of the company.

Appellant Wuhu Huarong Xingshang Investment Partnership (Limited Partnership) (hereinafter referred to as Huarong Xingshang) filed an appeal against the Civil Ruling (2018) Jing Min Chu No. 126-3 of the Beijing High People's Court concerning a dispute over a loan contract with Appellees Huangshan Huangshan District Mingren International Artists Manor Real Estate Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Huangshan Mingren Manor), Nanjing Longchang Real Estate Development Group Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Nanjing Longchang Company), Zhu Jinlong, Zhang Jianhe, China Zhongshi Financial Group Limited (hereinafter referred to as Zhongshi Financial Company), Liu Jieshan, and Third Parties at First Instance Huarong Emerging Industry Investment Management Co., Ltd. (formerly Huarong Emerging Industry Investment Management Co., Ltd.) (hereinafter referred to as Huarong Emerging Company), Wuhu Huarong Xingrong Investment Partnership (Limited Partnership) (hereinafter referred to as Huarong Xingrong), Zhongshi Enterprise Development (Jiangsu) Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Zhongshi Jiangsu Company), and Qinlai Investment Asset Management (Shanghai) Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Qinlaitou Company). This Court accepted the case and, in accordance with the law, formed a collegial panel to hear the case. The case is now concluded.

Huarong Xingshang filed the following claims before the court of first instance: 1. A judgment ordering Huangshan Mingren Manor to pay Huarong Xingshang the loan principal of RMB 571.55 million; 2. A judgment ordering Huangshan Mingren Manor to pay Huarong Xingshang liquidated damages of RMB 137.172 million; 3. A judgment ordering Nanjing Longchang Company, Zhu Jinlong, Zhang Jianhe, Zhongshi Financial Company, and Liu Jieshan to assume joint and several guaranty liability for the debts under the above claims 1 and 2; 4. A judgment that, with respect to the above claims 1 and 2, Huarong Xingshang has the right to be paid in priority from the real property of Huangshan Mingren Manor that has been registered for mortgage; 5. A judgment that the litigation costs, preservation fees, preservation guarantee fees, appraisal fees, travel expenses of relevant personnel, attorney fees, and other reasonable expenses incurred by Huarong Xingshang in realizing the claims shall be borne jointly by Huangshan Mingren Manor, Nanjing Longchang Company, Zhu Jinlong, Zhang Jianhe, Zhongshi Financial Company, and Liu Jieshan.

During the trial of this case, Qinlaitou Company submitted an "Objection Application" to the court of first instance on March 13, 2019, asserting that Huarong Emerging Company had no right to unilaterally file this lawsuit in the name of Huarong Xingshang.

On July 5, 2019, Qinlaitou Company and Zhongshi Jiangsu Company respectively submitted "Applications" to the court of first instance with substantially identical content, requesting: 1. To be allowed to intervene as third parties in this lawsuit; 2. To remove the managing partner authority of Huarong Emerging Company; 3. To order the dissolution and liquidation of Huarong Xingshang; 4. To rule to dismiss the lawsuit filed by Huarong Xingshang.

The court of first instance found that, according to the business registration information of Huarong Xingshang, Huarong Xingshang was established on March 27, 2017, and its enterprise type is a limited partnership. On December 25, 2017, the general partner Huarong Emerging Company, the general partner Qinlaitou Company, the senior limited partner Huarong Xingrong, and the junior limited partner Zhongshi Jiangsu Company jointly entered into the "Partnership Agreement of Wuhu Huarong Xingshang Investment Partnership (Limited Partnership)" (No. Huarong Emerging-2017-068-016) (hereinafter referred to as the "Partnership Agreement"), which stipulates: ... Article 5 Rights and Obligations of Partners 5.1 The basic rights of partners are as follows: ... (5) To attend the meetings of all partners and exercise voting rights based on their actual capital contributions. Article 6 Managing Partner 6.1 Managing Partner. 6.1.1 The general partner Huarong Emerging Company and the general partner Qinlaitou Company jointly serve as the managing partners of this limited partnership. The managing partners have the right to invest, manage, use, and dispose of the partnership property, and shall accept the supervision of other general partners and limited partners. 6.1.2 The partnership affairs of this limited partnership shall be executed by the managing partners. All acts taken by the managing partners to execute partnership affairs in accordance with the Partnership Enterprise Law and this Agreement are binding on this limited partnership. 6.2 Conditions and Selection Procedure for Managing Partners 6.2.2 All partners, by signing this Agreement, unanimously select the general partner Huarong Emerging Company and the general partner Qinlaitou Company to jointly serve as the managing partners of this limited partnership. 6.3 Authority of the Managing Partners The managing partners have the exclusive and exclusive execution rights for the partnership affairs as provided by the Partnership Enterprise Law and this Agreement, including but not limited to: ... (18) To initiate, respond to, or defend lawsuits or arbitrations for the benefit of this limited partnership, to negotiate and settle with counterparties in disputes, and to take all reasonable and necessary actions in a timely manner to protect the property safety of this limited partnership and to reduce risks that may be brought to the partners and their property due to the business activities of this limited partnership. 8.3 Voting Methods of the Partnership Meeting The partnership meeting shall be voted by all partners in proportion to their respective actual capital contributions. All matters specified in Article 8.4 of this Agreement must be approved by all partners who have made actual capital contributions to be adopted at the partnership meeting. 8.4 Functions and Powers of the Partnership Meeting The following matters of the partnership enterprise shall be resolved by the partnership meeting: (1) Review and approve the annual report of the managing partners; (2) Amend or supplement this Agreement; (3) Review and approve the transfer of a general partner's property interest in the limited partnership (except transfers to its affiliates); (4) Review and approve the pledge of a partner's property interest in the limited partnership to a third party; (5) Review and approve the cancellation, change, or similar operation of any seal of this partnership; (6) Review and approve the increase of capital contributions by existing partners to the partnership; (7) Review and approve the removal or change of the general partner or managing partner; (8) Review and approve the conversion between general partners and limited partners; (9) Review and approve the admission and withdrawal of partners and the inheritance of partner status; (10) Decide on the dissolution and liquidation of this partnership; (11) Review and approve the provision of guarantees in the name of the partnership and external borrowing of the partnership; (12) Decide to extend or shorten the term of the partnership or the investment period; (13) Other matters that laws and regulations require to be decided by the partnership meeting.

In accordance with the above Partnership Agreement, both managing partners of Huarong Xingshang, Huarong Emerging Company and Qinlaitou Company, have the right to initiate lawsuits for the benefit of the partnership. Since Qinlaitou Company submitted an "Objection Application" to the court of first instance during the trial regarding the matter of Huarong Emerging Company filing this lawsuit on behalf of Huarong Xingshang, and another partner, Zhongshi Jiangsu Company, also submitted an "Application" to the court of first instance, both expressing disagreement with this matter, and arguing that Huarong Xingshang's status as the plaintiff in this case is not appropriate, and the four partners of Huarong Xingshang could not reach a unanimous opinion on this matter, the court of first instance, in accordance with Article 56 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, notified the four partners of Huarong Xingshang — Huarong Emerging Company, Qinlaitou Company, Huarong Xingrong, and Zhongshi Jiangsu Company — to participate in the lawsuit as third parties. When the four partners of Huarong Xingshang still could not reach a unanimous opinion on the matter of Huarong Emerging Company representing Huarong Xingshang in filing this lawsuit, the court of first instance, in accordance with the relevant provisions of the Partnership Enterprise Law of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter referred to as the "Partnership Enterprise Law") and the above Partnership Agreement, ordered Huarong Xingshang to convene a meeting of all partners to vote and decide on the litigation matter. On October 11, 2021, Huarong Xingshang held the first interim partner meeting of 2021 and passed a resolution, the main content of which was as follows: In accordance with the Partnership Enterprise Law, the Partnership Agreement numbered "Huarong Emerging-2017-068-016", and the supplementary agreement numbered "Huarong Emerging-2017-068-017", the partners of Huarong Xingshang convened an interim partner meeting at 10:00 a.m. on October 11, 2021, in Conference Room 518, Huarong Huitong Asset Management Co., Ltd., North Building, No. A2, Baiwanzhuang Street, Xicheng District, Beijing. There were a total of 4 partners. The general partner Huarong Emerging Company, the general partner Qinlaitou Company, the senior limited partner Huarong Xingrong, and the junior limited partner Zhongshi Jiangsu Company all attended the meeting. The subscribed capital contributions of the attending partners accounted for 100% of the total subscribed capital contributions of all partners of the partnership, and the actual capital contributions of the attending partners accounted for 100% of the total actual capital contributions of all partners of the partnership. The convening of this partner meeting complied with the Partnership Agreement and relevant legal requirements. According to the voting mechanism set forth in Articles 8.3 and 8.4 of the Partnership Agreement, the matters considered at this partner meeting were voted on by all partners, and were approved by partners whose actual capital contributions accounted for 71.43% of the total actual capital contributions of all partners, constituting a valid and legally effective vote. Following the vote, the following resolutions were passed at this partner meeting: 1. Given that the borrower Huangshan Mingren Manor failed to repay the loan of RMB 571.55 million under the "Entrusted Loan Loan Contract" (Contract No. Huarong Emerging-2017-068-002) and the "Supplementary Agreement to the Entrusted Loan Loan Contract" (Contract No. Huarong Emerging-2017-068-003), and the related guarantors also failed to assume joint and several guaranty liability, in order to protect the lawful rights and interests of the partnership and all partners, it was resolved to approve the filing of a lawsuit by this partnership against the borrower Huangshan Mingren Manor and the guarantors Nanjing Longchang Company, Zhu Jinlong, Zhang Jianhe, Zhongshi Financial Company, and Liu Jieshan, to recover the claims against the debtor and guarantors through litigation. 2. It was resolved to approve and authorize the managing partner Huarong Emerging Company to handle matters related to the litigation. Huarong Emerging Company and Huarong Xingrong affixed their company seals and the name seals of their authorized representatives to the resolution, while Qinlaitou Company and Zhongshi Jiangsu Company did not sign or seal. The voting slips for the first interim partner meeting of Huarong Xingshang in 2021 showed: Huarong Emerging Company and Huarong Xingrong voted in favor, while Qinlaitou Company and Zhongshi Jiangsu Company voted against.

Subsequently, the litigation representatives of Huarong Xingshang and Huarong Xingrong submitted relevant legal opinions to the court of first instance, stating: With respect to the voting matter considered at this partner meeting, partners Huarong Emerging Company and Huarong Xingrong, whose actual capital contributions account for 71.43% of the total actual capital contributions of all partners, voted in favor, while partners Qinlaitou Company and Zhongshi Jiangsu Company, whose actual capital contributions account for 28.57% of the total actual capital contributions of all partners, voted against. Pursuant to Article 30 of the Partnership Enterprise Law, "Partners shall make resolutions on matters related to the partnership in accordance with the voting method stipulated in the partnership agreement. If the partnership agreement does not stipulate or stipulates unclearly, a voting method of one vote per partner and approval by more than half of all partners shall be adopted. Where this Law has separate provisions on voting methods of partnerships, such provisions shall apply." Only when the partnership agreement has no stipulation or an unclear stipulation on the voting method for a resolution matter of the partnership shall the voting method of one vote per partner and approval by more than half of all partners be applied. Given that Article 5.1 "Basic Rights of Partners" item (5) of the Partnership Agreement clearly stipulates that partners exercise voting rights at partner meetings based on their actual capital contributions, and Article 8.3 "Voting Methods of the Partnership Meeting" clearly stipulates that the voting method of the partner meeting is "all partners shall exercise voting rights in proportion to their respective actual capital contributions," and Article 8.4 "Functions and Powers of the Partnership Meeting" clearly lists the exceptional circumstances requiring approval by all partners, and since the matter resolved at this partner meeting does not fall within the exceptional circumstances requiring unanimous consent of all partners as stipulated in Article 8.4 of the Partnership Agreement, the voting on this resolution at this partner meeting should be based on the proportion of actual capital contributions of all partners, and the one-vote-per-partner voting method should not apply. According to the principle of majority rule, the resolution at this partner meeting only needs to be approved by partners whose actual capital contributions account for more than half of the total actual capital contributions of all partners to be adopted. Given that this resolution at this partner meeting was approved by partners whose actual capital contributions account for 71.43%, i.e., approved by partners holding 71.43% of the voting rights, the resolution was validly and legally adopted.

On January 13, 2021, the Huangshan District People's Court of Huangshan City, Anhui Province, sent a "Notice" (2020) Wan 1003 Po 9-1 to the court of first instance, informing that the court ruled on December 14, 2020, to accept the bankruptcy liquidation case of Huangshan Mingren Manor, and on December 16, 2020, issued a "Decision" (2020) Wan 1003 Po 9, appointing Anhui Zhongwan Law Firm as the administrator.

The court of first instance held that Article 29, paragraph 1 of the Partnership Enterprise Law provides: "Where partners separately execute partnership affairs, the executing partner may raise objections to the affairs executed by other partners. When raising an objection, execution of such affairs shall be suspended. If a dispute arises, a decision shall be made in accordance with Article 30 of this Law." To promote the smooth conduct of partnership business activities and leverage the strengths of each partner, pursuant to the partnership agreement or a decision of all partners, certain affairs of the partnership enterprise may be entrusted to one or several partners for separate execution. However, when executing separately, the executing partner may inevitably have instances of insufficient consideration or improper execution, and it cannot be ruled out that individual partners may fail to act with good faith, prudence, and diligence in handling the partnership affairs entrusted to them. In such circumstances, if the executing partner's conduct is improper or erroneous, to the detriment of the partnership enterprise's interests, the executing partner may raise objections to the affairs executed by other partners. The right to raise objections is not only an inviolable statutory right of the executing partner but also a restriction on the rights of other partners. It embodies the partner's supervisory power over the execution of partnership affairs and is the fundamental guarantee for safeguarding the common interests of the partnership enterprise, i.e., all partners. At the same time, when an executing partner raises an objection to the affairs executed by other partners, execution of such affairs shall also be suspended, i.e., to prevent the possibility that other partners may ignore the objection raised, thereby avoiding potential aggravation of damage to the partnership enterprise. In this case, Qin Lai Tou Company, as one of the executing partners of Huarong Xingshang, submitted an "Objection Application" to the court of first instance regarding Huarong Xinxing Company's initiation of this lawsuit on behalf of Huarong Xingshang, expressing disagreement with this matter and asserting that Huarong Xingshang lacked standing as the plaintiff in this case. Therefore, pursuant to the above provision of the Partnership Enterprise Law, Huarong Xinxing Company should suspend the execution of the litigation matter in this case. When a dispute arises among the partners of Huarong Xingshang concerning this litigation matter, a relevant decision should be made in accordance with Article 30 of the Partnership Enterprise Law.

Article 30, paragraph 1 of the Partnership Enterprise Law provides: "Where partners make resolutions on matters relating to the partnership enterprise, the voting method shall be handled in accordance with the voting procedures stipulated in the partnership agreement. If the partnership agreement does not stipulate or the stipulation is unclear, the voting method shall be one vote per partner and approval by more than half of all partners." Partnership affairs may be jointly executed by all partners, and "joint execution" means joint decision-making. Matters decided jointly include cases where all partners unanimously agree and cases where a majority of partners agree, which depends on the relevant provisions of the law or the stipulations of the partnership agreement. To fully respect partner autonomy, when partners make resolutions on matters relating to the partnership enterprise, the voting method shall be handled in accordance with the voting procedures stipulated in the partnership agreement. Except where the law has clear provisions or the partnership agreement provides otherwise, when the partnership agreement does not stipulate or the stipulation is unclear, given that partners may have varying capital contributions to the partnership enterprise and that general partners, other than limited partners, bear unlimited joint and several liability for the partnership enterprise's debts, to protect partners with smaller capital contributions, Article 30, paragraph 1 of the Partnership Enterprise Law provides that in such circumstances, the voting method shall be one vote per partner and approval by more than half of all partners. It should be noted that the personal nature of the partnership enterprise determines that resolutions made based on the majority opinion of partners on matters relating to the partnership enterprise cannot harm the interests of minority or individual partners. Moreover, the application of the majority rule principle to vote on matters relating to the partnership enterprise should generally be limited to routine affairs in the partnership enterprise's operations, and handling major issues of the partnership enterprise should not fall under this category. In this case, although Article 5.1(5) of the partnership agreement stipulates that partners shall exercise their voting rights based on their actual paid-in capital contributions when attending partner meetings, and Article 8.3 stipulates that the voting method at partner meetings shall be "all partners exercise their voting rights in proportion to their respective actual paid-in capital contributions," Article 8.3 of the partnership agreement also stipulates that "all matters stipulated in Article 8.4 of this agreement must be approved by all partners who have made actual paid-in capital contributions before they can be passed at the partner meeting." Article 8.4(13) regarding the functions and powers of the partner meeting stipulates "other matters that shall be decided by the partner meeting as provided by laws and regulations." According to Article 6.3(18) of the partnership agreement, both executing partners of Huarong Xingshang, Huarong Xinxing Company and Qin Lai Tou Company, have the right to initiate litigation for the benefit of the partnership enterprise. Initiating litigation is not a routine affair in the partnership enterprise's operations and should be considered a major issue affecting the partnership enterprise's interests. Since the partnership agreement does not provide for the handling method if the two executing partners have a dispute over this matter, it should be deemed as a situation where "the partnership agreement does not stipulate or the stipulation is unclear" as provided in Article 30, paragraph 1 of the Partnership Enterprise Law. Now, Qin Lai Tou Company has submitted an "Objection Application" to the court of first instance regarding Huarong Xinxing Company's initiation of this lawsuit on behalf of Huarong Xingshang, expressing disagreement with this matter and asserting that Huarong Xingshang lacks standing as the plaintiff in this case. The four partners of Huarong Xingshang have also failed to form a unanimous opinion on this matter. In such circumstances, the litigation matter in this case should be voted on in accordance with Article 30, paragraph 1 of the Partnership Enterprise Law, which provides that "if the partnership agreement does not stipulate or the stipulation is unclear, the voting method shall be one vote per partner and approval by more than half of all partners." Since Huarong Xinxing Company and Huarong Xingrong both cast affirmative votes, while Qin Lai Tou Company and Zhongshi Jiangsu Company both cast negative votes, the statutory condition of approval by more than half of all partners has not been met, and thus the resolution of this partner meeting was not adopted. Accordingly, the court of first instance did not accept the opinion of Huarong Xingshang's agent ad litem that "the vote on the resolution of this partner meeting should be conducted in proportion to the actual paid-in capital contributions of all partners, and the one-vote-per-partner voting method does not apply. According to the majority rule principle, the resolution of this partner meeting only needs to be approved by partners whose actual paid-in capital contributions account for more than half of the total actual paid-in capital contributions of all partners. Since the resolution of this partner meeting has been approved by partners whose actual paid-in capital contributions account for 71.43%, i.e., approved by partners holding 71.43% of the voting rights, the resolution of this partner meeting has been lawfully and effectively adopted."

In summary, given that the partnership agreement involved in this case does not provide for the handling method after a dispute arises between the two executing partners of the partnership enterprise Huarong Xingshang regarding Huarong Xinxing Company's initiation of this lawsuit on behalf of Huarong Xingshang, and the resolution adopted by Huarong Xingshang at the first interim partner meeting in 2021 was not approved by more than half of all partners, and the four partners of Huarong Xingshang have still failed to form a unanimous opinion on this matter, Huarong Xinxing Company does not have the right to unilaterally initiate this lawsuit on behalf of Huarong Xingshang, and this lawsuit should not be deemed as Huarong Xingshang's true expression of intent. Pursuant to Article 154, paragraph 1(3) and Article 169, paragraph 1 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the ruling is as follows: The lawsuit of Huarong Xingshang is dismissed.

Huarong Xingshang, dissatisfied with the first-instance ruling, appealed to this Court, contending that: (1) Article 6.3 of the Partnership Agreement clearly stipulates that the authority of the executing partner includes initiating litigation for the benefit of the partnership enterprise and reducing risks that the partnership enterprise's business activities may bring to the partners and their property. When the partnership enterprise's debtor and guarantor refused to repay the loan principal of RMB 571.55 million and corresponding interest, the executing partner Huarong Xinxing Company initiated this lawsuit in the name of the partnership enterprise Huarong Xingshang, which is not only the right granted by the Partnership Enterprise Law and the Partnership Agreement but also the obligation Huarong Xinxing Company must assume. In addition, Article 8.3 of the Partnership Agreement stipulates that the voting method at partner meetings is "all partners exercise their voting rights in proportion to their respective actual paid-in capital contributions." The resolution of this meeting does not apply the one-vote-per-partner voting method, and it only needs to be approved by partners whose actual paid-in capital contributions account for more than half of the total actual paid-in capital contributions of all partners. The court of first instance, relying on Article 30 of the Partnership Enterprise Law, held that Huarong Xinxing Company's initiation of this lawsuit in the name of Huarong Xingshang requires approval by more than half of all partners on a one-vote-per-partner basis, which is an error in applying the law. Therefore, the first-instance ruling that Huarong Xinxing Company does not have the right to unilaterally initiate this lawsuit on behalf of Huarong Xingshang and that this lawsuit should not be deemed as Huarong Xingshang's true expression of intent lacks factual and legal basis. (2) Qin Lai Tou Company's objection to this lawsuit is aimed at evading the pursuit of guarantor liability against Liu Jieshan and Zhongshi Financial Company, who have a direct interest relationship with the partnership enterprise. This objection seriously harms the interests of the partnership enterprise and other partners and is inconsistent with the identity and duties of an executing partner. The court of first instance's application of Article 29 of the Partnership Enterprise Law to support its objection is an error in applying the law. (3) The representative of partner Zhongshi Jiangsu Company, Liu Jieshan, and the legal representative of executing partner Qin Lai Tou Company, Yang Huaijun, have a direct interest in this case. The acts of these two persons participating in the partner meeting and exercising voting rights on behalf of Zhongshi Jiangsu Company and Qin Lai Tou Company, respectively, are invalid. (4) According to the legal application of the court of first instance, if all partners cannot form a unanimous opinion, the partnership enterprise cannot initiate litigation. This undoubtedly directly deprives the partnership enterprise of its right to sue, both procedurally and substantively, and contradicts the spirit of derivative actions that limited partners can initiate, as provided in Article 68 of the Partnership Enterprise Law and recognized in judicial practice, and is also inconsistent with the spirit of "all cases must be accepted" and "all lawsuits must be entertained." In summary, Huarong Xingshang requests the revocation of the first-instance ruling and an order for the court of first instance to hear the case.

Zhongshi Jiangsu Company submitted its opinion to this Court, contending that: (1) Qin Lai Tou Company and Huarong Xinxing Company are both executing partners of Huarong Xingshang and have the same authority. Huarong Xinxing Company, taking advantage of its convenience in managing the partnership enterprise's official seal, unilaterally manipulated Huarong Xingshang to initiate litigation, apply for preservation, and appeal against Huangshan Celebrity Manor, seriously infringing upon the rights of other partners of the partnership enterprise. This lawsuit cannot be deemed as Huarong Xingshang's true expression of intent. (2) Huarong Xinxing Company unilaterally used the partnership enterprise Huarong Xingshang's official seal to initiate this lawsuit and apply for pre-litigation preservation, and without the consent of Zhongshi Jiangsu Company, declared the principal debt of RMB 571.55 million as RMB 2,132.32 million, obstructing the bankruptcy liquidation process. Huarong Xinxing Company's affiliate Huarong Xingrong did not make full capital contributions, and Huarong Xinxing Company did not demand capital contributions and overdue contribution liquidated damages from it. Its omission harmed the interests of the partnership enterprise. (3) The root cause of the inability of all partners to reach a unanimous opinion is that Huarong Xinxing Company only considered the interests of the priority partner Huarong Xingrong and did not consider the interests of the partnership enterprise. In summary, Huarong Xingshang's appeal claims are untenable and should be dismissed.

This Court holds that although Article 6.3(18) of the Partnership Agreement, "Authority of Executing Partners," stipulates that both executing partners of Huarong Xingshang, Huarong Xinxing Company and Qin Lai Tou Company, have the right to initiate litigation for the benefit of the partnership enterprise, after Huarong Xinxing Company initiated the lawsuit in the name of the partnership enterprise, other partners, including Qin Lai Tou Company, raised objections as to whether Huarong Xinxing Company had the authority to initiate the lawsuit on behalf of the partnership enterprise. Huarong Xingshang then convened a partner meeting to make a resolution on whether to initiate this lawsuit. The issue in dispute in this case is whether the voting method for the above resolution complies with the requirements of the Partnership Agreement or relevant legal provisions and whether one of the executing partners, Huarong Xinxing Company, is entitled to initiate this lawsuit in the name of the partnership enterprise Huarong Xingshang based on the resolution.

Qin Lai Tou Company, as one of the executing partners of Huarong Xingshang, raised an objection to Huarong Xinxing Company's initiation of this lawsuit on behalf of Huarong Xingshang, asserting that Huarong Xingshang lacks standing as the plaintiff in this case. The above facts indicate that a dispute has arisen among the partners regarding the execution of partnership affairs. According to Article 29, paragraph 1 of the Partnership Enterprise Law, where partners separately execute partnership affairs, the executing partner may raise objections to the affairs executed by other partners. When raising an objection, execution of such affairs shall be suspended. If a dispute arises, a decision shall be made in accordance with Article 30 of the Partnership Enterprise Law. The resolutions made by partners on matters relating to the partnership enterprise are directed at partnership affairs. To fully respect party autonomy, partners may stipulate specific voting methods for matters relating to the partnership enterprise in the partnership agreement. According to Article 30 of the Partnership Enterprise Law, unless otherwise provided by law, where the partnership agreement does not stipulate or the stipulation is unclear regarding the voting matter and the corresponding voting method, when partners make resolutions on matters relating to the partnership enterprise, the voting method shall be one vote per partner and approval by more than half of all partners.

Article 8.3 of the Partnership Agreement in this case stipulates two voting methods at partner meetings: "all partners exercise their voting rights in proportion to their respective actual paid-in capital contributions" and "all matters stipulated in Article 8.4 must be approved by all partners who have made actual paid-in capital contributions before they can be passed at the partner meeting." From the content of Article 8.4 of the Partnership Agreement, the voting matters it covers are specifically related to major interests of the partnership enterprise. However, the matters requiring approval by all partners, as stipulated in that article, do not include the litigation dispute in this case. Article 8.3 of the Partnership Agreement does not specify the specific content of voting matters. Whether the voting method stipulated in Article 8.3 of the Partnership Agreement can be applied to the disputed matter in this case should be comprehensively determined in light of the content of Article 8.4 of the Partnership Agreement and the nature of the partnership enterprise. Whether a partnership enterprise initiates litigation over a legal dispute arising in its operations concerns relatively significant operational interests of the partnership enterprise and cannot be simply categorized as routine affairs in the partnership enterprise's activities. Where a dispute arises between the two executing partners of the partnership enterprise on this matter, applying the capital majority rule for voting on such a resolution is not conducive to protecting the interests of minority investors and does not reflect the personal nature of the partnership enterprise. Therefore, the voting method for the disputed matter in this case should not be construed as falling within the scope of the stipulation in Article 8.3 of the Partnership Agreement that "all partners exercise their voting rights in proportion to their respective actual paid-in capital contributions." Huarong Xingshang's appeal ground that Article 8.3 of the Partnership Agreement regarding "all partners exercise their voting rights in proportion to their respective actual paid-in capital contributions" should apply is not accepted by this Court. Since the Partnership Agreement does not stipulate a specific and clear voting method for the disputed matter in this case, in accordance with Article 30 of the Partnership Enterprise Law, the voting method shall be one vote per partner and approval by more than half of all partners. Although Huarong Xingshang convened a partner meeting on whether to initiate litigation, the resolution adopted was not approved by more than half of all partners. The court of first instance accordingly held that Huarong Xinxing Company does not have the right to unilaterally initiate this lawsuit on behalf of Huarong Xingshang, that this lawsuit should not be deemed as Huarong Xingshang's true expression of intent, and ruled to dismiss Huarong Xingshang's lawsuit. This ruling has factual and legal basis and is upheld by this Court.

As for the purpose of Qin Lai Tou Company's objection to this lawsuit and whether such objection harms the interests of the partnership enterprise and other partners, these are unrelated to the issue of standing to sue in dispute in this case. Although Huarong Xingshang asserts that Liu Jieshan, the representative of Zhongshi Jiangsu Company, and Yang Huaijun, the legal representative of Qin Lai Tou Company, have a direct interest in this case and that the acts of these two persons representing Zhongshi Jiangsu Company and Qin Lai Tou Company in participating in the partner meeting and exercising voting rights are invalid, Huarong Xingshang has not submitted any evidence to prove this, and this Court does not support this assertion.

This case involves a dispute between the two executing partners of the partnership enterprise over whether to initiate this lawsuit. Where the resolution made at the partner meeting on the disputed matter was not approved by more than half of all partners, the issue is whether one of the executing partners, Huarong Xinxing Company, has the right to initiate this lawsuit in the name of the partnership enterprise Huarong Xingshang. The above situation is different from the scenario under Article 68 of the Partnership Enterprise Law, where a limited partner may "when the executing partner neglects to exercise its rights, urge it to exercise its rights, or initiate a lawsuit in its own name for the benefit of the enterprise." In this case, there is no situation where Huarong Xinxing Company initiated a lawsuit in its own name. Huarong Xingshang's assertion that the first-instance ruling directly deprives the partnership enterprise of its right to sue and contradicts the spirit of derivative actions that limited partners can initiate lacks basis and is not supported by this Court.

In summary, the first-instance ruling has clear findings of fact and correct application of law. This Court, in accordance with Article 177, paragraph 1, item 1 and Article 178 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China (as amended in 2021), renders the following ruling:

The appeal is dismissed and the first-instance ruling is affirmed.

This ruling is final.
